title: Memory Leak in Docker 27.0.3
body:
### Description

After I updated to Docker 27.0.3 (I do not remember what was the older version, sorry, I upgraded my dedicated servers when the RegreSSHion exploit happened, but technically the older version is a version between 10/01/2024 (when the system was installed) and 01/07/2024 (when I upgraded all packages)) the `dockerd` daemon is leaking memory like crazy, in two of my dedicated servers `dockerd` ends up eating so much memory that containers end up getting OOM'd by the system

![image](https://github.com/moby/moby/assets/9496359/3e257f9c-bef9-436f-ba7e-be2806b81394)

If I restart Docker, the `dockerd` memory usage drops to ~200MB, and then keeps increasing and increasing and increasing...

### Reproduce

*I don't know how to reproduce this yet*

### Expected behavior

That `dockerd` does not eating up so much memory.

### docker version

```bash
Docker version 27.0.3, build 7d4bcd8
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
There is only one dedicated server that I have that isn't affected by that memory leak, but that dedicated server only has two  containers running, and both are PostgreSQL containers. They have another key difference that other dedicated servers do not have: none of the two containers running on that dedicated server have health probes (Docker Compose's `healthcheck`) set up.

```yml
version: "3.9"
services:
  powercms:
    image: ghcr.io/mrpowergamerbr/powercms@participant12:22262da1468bb3bdd775027da3b2d6cdcaf69859fa1c9b245d414713b4b4b093
    network_mode: service:tailscale
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: ./content/
        target: /content
    environment:
      JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: "-verbose:gc -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -Xmx1G -Xms1G -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/br/"] # What command will be used to check if the system is healthy or not
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    depends_on:
      tailscale:
        condition: service_healthy
  tailscale:
    hostname: powercms
    image: tailscale/tailscale:latest
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "tailscale status"]
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 60
    volumes:
      - "./tailscale_var_lib:/var/lib"
      - "/dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun"
    cap_add:
      - net_admin
      - sys_module
      - net_raw
    command: tailscaled
```

Could it be related to health checks? A lot of my containers are set up like this, with a Tailscale service container running alongside it.

But then again, the heap dump shows that it is something related to http requests, so it is probably not it... but idk I don't know about go.

It could also be logs, I use the `local` driver and I have some very "chatty" applications on the affected dedicated servers.

Lookling at your heap dumps on a bigger screen I'd guess you likely have tracing enabled but either can't connect to the exporter (so they just accumulate) or you have a bunch of tracing spans actively running.
Can you get a goroutine dump as well?

Same basic curlc ommand just change `/heap` to `/goroutine?debug=2`
```
curl -v --silent -XGET --unix-socket /run/docker.sock http://localhost/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I don't know why the buildkit tracing (used for the buildkit history API) is so bloated but I have an idea as to why the main otel exporter may be.
I see a lot of long running requests (container attach, events), I suspect these are long-running spans that never end until the request is terminated. OTel is holding onto that data until the spans end.
I'll run some tests locally to see if that's was causing the excessive memory usage.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I see a lot of long running requests (container attach, events)

Once again I’m coming with theories that may be wrong, but that may be useful when debugging the issue:

On my servers I run my containers with “docker compose up” (*not* detached), they are managed by systemd.

Could it be that the “long running events” are because Compose automatically tails the container logs when running? This would explain about why my dedicated server that has a lot of containers is “more affected” (memory fills up faster) than my other dedicated servers that has less containers.

But then again I think that this may not be it, because in that case my other dedicated server that only has PostgreSQL containers would also be affected.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> I don't know why the buildkit tracing (used for the buildkit history API) is so bloated but I have an idea as to why the main otel exporter may be.
I see a lot of long running requests (container attach, events),

Looking at the current setup, everything that goes to the global tracer is also sent to the buildkit tracer. If there are spans that do not end, then they are just kept in memory forever.

Edit: actually no, they would only be kept if the traceID of the span matches ongoing builds traceID. So I still think early shutdown is the best explanation.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Some findings: One of my dedicated servers was installed on 03/04/2024, so this narrows down the versions a bit. I tried downgrading from Docker 27.0.3 to Docker 26.0.2, but it seems that the issue also affects 26.0.2 too... HOWEVER I had only downgraded the `docker-ce` package and the `docker-ce-cli` package, not the `containerd.io` + `docker-buildx-plugin` + `docker-compose-plugin`. Maybe these three packages can also cause the memory leak? The daemon got up to 1GB of usage before I killed it.

Then I attempted to downgrade Docker to 26.0.0, which was the version that was the most recent version at the time I installed Ubuntu Server 22.04 on that dedicated server, but this time I tried matching all package versions to avoid any possible issues.

```bash
sudo apt-get purge docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin docker-ce-rootless-extras
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/containerd

VERSION_STRING=5:26.0.0-1~ubuntu.22.04~jammy
BUILDX_VERSION_STRING=0.13.1-1~ubuntu.22.04~jammy
COMPOSE_VERSION_STRING=2.25.0-1~ubuntu.22.04~jammy
CONTAINERD_VERSION_STRING=1.6.33-1

sudo apt-get install docker-ce=$VERSION_STRING docker-ce-cli=$VERSION_STRING containerd.io=$CONTAINERD_VERSION_STRING docker-buildx-plugin=$BUILDX_VERSION_STRING docker-compose-plugin=$COMPOSE_VERSION_STRING
```

And now it worked! I kept Docker running for ~2 hours and `dockerd`'s memory usage has stayed around ~300MB.

Yes, this is a temporary solution because no one wants to run outdated software, but this may be useful for anyone that is having issues with the memory leaks and needs a solution right now.

If any other outstanding issues happen, then I will talk about it here, but for now at least there is a "known good" Docker version that is not affected by the memory leak: Docker 26.0.0

And here's how to hold the version after it is installed: `apt-mark hold docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The healthchecks will definitely create more spans, however I have not been able to reproduce the issue locally.
I do see dockerd's RSS creep up (I'm running 50 containers all with healthchecks at 2s intervals) but this is not reflected in the heap.
The Buildkit tracer does creep up a bit as well (enough to make it to the top 10 inuse space, but this is ~7MB total size), but it will drop back down on its own.

I've tried with
- tracing enabled and exporting properly to an OTLP endpoint.
- tracing enabled but the OTLP endpoint is fake so it gets connection refused
- tracing completely disabled

Here is a test script, which I've had a few different variations of, none seem to produce particularly different results:

```bash
set -eu -o pipefail

count=50
if [ -v 1 ] && [ -n "$1" ]; then
    count="${1}"
fi

doTimes() {
    local count=$1
    shift;

    for i in $(seq $count); do
        $@ > /dev/null &
    done
}

cleanup() {
    set +e

    echo Cleaning up... >&2

    jobs -p | xargs -r kill
    wait

    echo Done cleaning up >&2
}

trap 'cleanup' EXIT

runCmd () {
    docker run --log-driver=none --health-cmd true --health-interval 2s --attach stdout --attach stderr --rm busybox sh -c 'while true; do usleep 10000; done'
}


echo Running ${count} jobs...
doTimes ${count} runCmd

echo Number of running jobs: $(jobs -p | wc -l)
echo Waiting...
```

The main thing here is that docker run command is creating 3 requests, 2 are persistent (attach and events), which the script will do 50 times (or whatever you specify).
Interrupting the script should cause all containers to exit and get auto-cleaned up by dockerd.

I am going to let this run for an extended period to see what happens.

@participant1 I was able to reproduce the issue on a virtual machine! I think this may be helpful to track down the issue :3 

**Virtual Machine Files (VirtualBox):** https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dMih816cthk7e3nKQZhz3ykfiv959Vba/view?usp=sharing

Username: `mrpowergamerbr`
Password: `dockertest`

(The root password is also `dockertest`)

**Notes:**
* Ubuntu Server 24.04, the only change I made on the installation was that the disk itself is just a plain old ext4 partition, no bells and whistles like LUKS or LVM.
* I changed some settings on the `docker.json`: The log driver is `local`, and the subnet IPs were also changed.
* The containers are "handled" by systemd, you can start all the services with `bash start_services.sh` script present inside `/srv`, and here's the service definition

```
[Unit]
Description=DockerTest
Requires=docker.service
After=docker.service
[Service]
# Required for it to restart automatically on exit
Restart=always
WorkingDirectory=/srv/dockertest1/
ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker compose up --abort-on-container-exit
ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker compose down
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

* The containers are all nginx containers with a valid healthcheck configured (it is just a curl command call that queries 127.0.0.1)
* Shutting down the containers DOES NOT clean up the memory used by the Docker Daemon.
* I still need to test this exact setup in Docker 26.0.0, to check if the memory leak ACTUALLY does not happen in this setup.
* It took around ~1 hour to 1GB to be "leaked" by the `dockerd` process - As a comparsion, on my production dedicated server that is running ~68 containers in Docker 26.0.0, `dockerd` uses only ~400MB.

comments.body:
And now a cool and useful finding that will help pin point down where the issue is..!

# Docker 27.0.1, using older compose/buildx/containerd.io versions [NOT AFFECTED BY THE LEAK]

I used the same versions that I used on the Docker 26.1.0 test for the `docker-buildx-plugin`, `docker-compose-plugin` and `containerd.io` packages... and that stopped the memory leak!

So maybe the issue isn't in moby (Docker Engine) itself, but in one of the other three packages. I don't think it is an issue in `containerd.io` because I had tried 27.0.3 with `containerd.io 1.6.33-1` when @participant4 asked about it, and it also had the memory leak. https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/48144#issuecomment-2230941155

If it is really an issue in the other packages, that would explain why when I downgraded Docker to 26.0.2 previously I still had the memory leak, because I didn't downgrade the compose/buildx/containerd.io packages then, whereas when I downgraded to 26.0.0 I did attempt to match all packages.

I would guess that Docker 27.0.3 will also not be affected by the memory leak, as long as you use the older buildx/compose/containerd.io versions, maybe I should try that out later...

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Same issue with Debian 12 and Docker 27.3.1. `dockerd` goes from taking **120 MB of RAM on start to 2 GB in a single day**, and after 2-3 days crashes my server due to memory exhaustion (on that machine there is 4 GB of RAM).
At the same time, the total RAM usage of the running containers never exceeded 800 MB, and only Docker and these containers run on that machine.

Thanks to @reporter's investigation, I could find the minimal solution. No need to restart the server, just do:
```bash
apt install docker-compose-plugin=2.26.1-1~debian.12~bookworm
apt-mark hold docker-compose-plugin
systemctl restart docker
```
At first I thought the issue would come from containerd.io or buildx, but no, it really seems to be coming from a Docker Compose incompatibility or something.

With this fix, `dockerd` varies between 115 and 140 MB of RAM over at least 5 days.

EDIT: I opened an issue about it on `docker-compose-plugin`, since downgrading it works around the issue.
